links.note: Variations help the species though not the individual - the survival value of variation thrown up during DNA copying (190), not the general importance of reproduction (189).
Benefits of reproducing by spores - dispersal, perennation, numbers (196).
Seminal vesicles and prostate are accessory glands of the male tract (201).
Embryo nourished through placenta and umbilical cord in the uterine wall - the uterus/implantation part of the female system (202); no separate placenta concept exists here.
Copper-T does not protect against STDs - the item contrasts two arms of 204, contraception and STD prevention.
Anther contains pollen grains - floral structure and the male part (198). 199 would be the transfer of that pollen.
Testis makes sperm and secretes testosterone - both functions of the male reproductive system (201).
Reasons for adopting contraception, including spacing and STD protection (204).
Diagram identified as tubectomy - a surgical contraceptive method (204), not female anatomy for its own sake (202).
Diagram of yeast with parent and bud - budding (193), not fission (192), because the daughter forms as an outgrowth.
Bryophyllum multiplies from adventitious buds in leaf notches - vegetative propagation (195).
Fertility period given as days 14-16 of the cycle - a fact about the menstrual cycle (203).
Labels the female tract and asks where egg production, fertilisation and implantation occur (202). The endometrial part (c) touches 203 but the item is built on the organ map.
A bisexual flower still fruits after its stamens are removed because cross-pollination supplies the pollen (199), not floral structure (198).
Chromosome number is kept constant because meiosis halves it in gametes and fertilisation restores it - the defining mechanics of sexual reproduction (197).
A vertically cut Planaria gives two whole animals - regeneration (194), distinct from fragmentation (193) because the cut is imposed, not a reproductive habit.
Male gamete 24, so female gamete 24 and zygote 48 - haploid gametes fusing to a diploid zygote (197).
Constancy across zygote, embryonal cells and adult is maintained by mitosis faithfully copying the DNA (190). 197 explains only the zygote's ploidy, not the later stages.
Where the zygote sits after fertilisation - in the embryo sac of the ovule (199).
Uterine changes when fertilisation fails: endometrium sloughs off as menstruation (203).
Uterine changes after implantation - thickened vascular endometrium forming the placenta (202), the opposite outcome from the menstruation item 86140.
Egg-to-zygote chromosome ratio 1:2 - haploid gamete to diploid zygote (197). The X/Y difference in the second half belongs to sex determination, which is another chapter.
Draw and label the four whorls and name the gamete-producing organs - floral structure (198).
What the placenta is and does in pregnancy - the uterus-and-embryo part of the female system (202).
Ways to avoid pregnancy, elaborated on barrier methods (204).
Fertilisation occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube - the site named in 202. The once-a-month framing rests on ovulation but the answer is about where and how fertilisation happens.
Describes STDs and their prevention (204).
Persuading a couple to limit family size - the family-planning arm of reproductive health (204).
Decorating the campus with Bougainvillea by preparing stem cuttings - vegetative propagation (195).
AIDS as a sexually transmitted disease and its causative HIV (204).
Full form of HIV, asked only as the agent of an STD (204).
Full form of IUCD - a contraceptive device (204).
The hormone behind the changes in girls at 10-12 years - puberty and sexual maturation (200), not the female organ map (202).
Jasmine is grown by layering - an artificial method of vegetative propagation (195).
No two individuals are alike because of variations arising in DNA copying during reproduction (190).
Names reproduction as the life process behind population growth - the importance-of-reproduction concept (189).
Germ cells of a flower sit in the anther and the ovule - floral structure (198).
Planaria cut in two regrows the missing parts - regeneration (194).
No fertilisation without pollination because pollen must first reach the stigma - the pollination-to-fertilisation sequence (199).
A long Spirogyra filament breaks into pieces that grow on - fragmentation (193), not regeneration (194), since no injury or lost part is involved.
Organisms bearing both sex organs, answered with the bisexual flower (mustard) - the unisexual/bisexual distinction taught with floral structure (198).
Names testis and ovary as the germ-cell producing organs. Filed on 201; the ovary half belongs to 202, and the item splits evenly between the two.
A bacterial and a viral STD with prevention (204).
Seminal vesicles, prostate and two testis functions - all male reproductive system (201).
Two functions of the copper-T: destroying sperm and preventing implantation (204).
Rhizopus multiplying through sporangia and spores (196).
Part (a) is Spirogyra fragmentation (193); part (b) is Planaria regeneration, which would be 194. Filed on 193 as the leading part - the item spans two concepts.
Why the testes hang in the scrotum - temperature regulation for sperm formation, a male-system design fact (201).

Chromosome numbers in egg, zygote, ENDOSPERM and leaf of tobacco: the triploid endosperm can only be explained by double fertilisation in the flowering plant (199), which is why this sits on 199 and the plain gamete item 86133 sits on 197.
Ovary ripens to fruit and ovule to seed, with plumule and radicle labelled - post-fertilisation development (199).
Placenta and its two roles in pregnancy (202).
Bacterial STDs plus how oral pills prevent pregnancy - both arms of 204.
